edits_summary: Created new module `thinkingCache.ts` (96 lines) — in-memory map keyed by sessionId storing { thinking, activeAt, userId } with 5s TTL. Exports recordThinking(), clearThinking(), getActivitySnapshotForUser().

Refactored `sessionUpdateHandler.ts` to extract each socket.on() callback into top-level helper functions (handleUpdateMetadata / handleUpdateState / handleSessionAlive / handleMessage / handleSessionEnd) so the exported function is 18 lines and each helper is <30 lines. This refactor was required to pass the pretool-quality-gate.py hook (function-size & nesting-depth thresholds). All semantics are preserved verbatim.
Added `recordThinking(sid, userId, thinking, t)` call inside performSessionAlive (after activityCache.queueSessionUpdate) so every session-alive heartbeat refreshes the per-session thinking cache.
Added `clearThinking(sid)` call inside performSessionEnd so a clean Stop transition wipes any stale thinking entry.

Refactored `socket.ts` — extracted handshake validation, connection building, lifecycle registration, and handler registration into top-level helpers. Replaced the inline machine-online broadcast with `broadcastConnectActivity(...)` which now also handles user-scoped connections.

Pipeline 7.2 core change: when a user-scoped socket connects, `sendSessionSnapshotsToConnectingSocket(socket, userId)` queries the user's recently-active sessions via thinkingCache.getActivitySnapshotForUser(), and emits one `ephemeral` payload per session directly to the connecting socket using the existing `buildSessionActivityEphemeral(sid, true, activeAt, thinking)` shape (per QA Objection #3 — no new event type).
thinking_source_decision: In-memory Map (`thinkingCache.ts`) with 5s TTL, keyed by sessionId, valued as { thinking, activeAt, userId }. Rationale: (1) BA spec / addendum Section 7.2 explicitly says 'Optional: short-TTL persistence of thinking so server can answer is-X-currently-thinking between heartbeats' — short-TTL was chosen, not Prisma. (2) Persistence in Prisma was ruled out by the spec explicitly: 'Modify Prisma schema (no schema migration in this pipeline — keep state in memory or short-TTL Redis)'. (3) Redis was considered but rejected because the server is single-process for the dev environment and adding Redis dependency increases blast radius. The Map can be swapped for a Redis cache later without changing the public API of `recordThinking/clearThinking/getActivitySnapshotForUser`. (4) The new module isolates the cache from the existing `activityCache` (sessionCache.ts) which has different semantics (cache-of-DB-validation vs cache-of-transient-flag) and different TTL.
ttl_decision: 5 seconds. Rationale: CLI keepAlive cadence is 2s (per packages/happy-cli/src/claude/session.ts:69-73 and apiSession.ts:523-533, confirmed by Codex research and QA spot-check). 2s × 2.5 = 5s gives a 1.5x safety margin so a freshly connecting client always sees the most recent in-flight state, while still expiring naturally if the CLI silences (e.g. process exit without session-end). The TTL is purposely SHORTER than the activityCache CACHE_TTL (30s) because thinking is much more transient than 'is the session valid'.
ephemeral_shape_used: activity (existing). Reused buildSessionActivityEphemeral(sid, active=true, activeAt, thinking) verbatim. No new event type, no new payload field. The connecting client's existing handleEphemeralUpdate at sync.ts already routes 'activity' → session.thinking & session.activeAt, so pipeline 7.3 does not need to add a new handler. This satisfies QA Objection #3 directly.
rationale: Implements Section 7.2 verbatim: 'on new socket connection, if any session's CLI is currently active=true, send the current ephemeral activity snapshot (thinking state if known) to the new client'. The pattern replicates socket.ts:103-112 (machine-connect snapshot) for user-scoped sessions, but emits to the connecting socket only (not broadcast) since other already-open tabs already have the live state. Combined with pipeline 7.1 (CLI emits fresh thinking on bg-task wake) and pipeline 7.3 (app-side reconnect catch-up wiring fix), this closes the observable gap where 'claude babbling' indicator disappears after web reopen.
type_check: pass (only pre-existing error in sessionCache.ts:42 remains — `Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'Timeout'` — UNRELATED to this pipeline; sessionCache.ts was not modified). All new code in thinkingCache.ts, socket.ts, and sessionUpdateHandler.ts compiles cleanly.
qa_notes: After all 3 pipelines (7.1 CLI / 7.2 server / 7.3 app) land, orchestrator must (a) rebuild happy-server-dev from worktree (`docker build -f Dockerfile.server-slim -t happy-server-dev:latest <WORKTREE>` + `cd /root/deploy && docker compose up -d happy-server-dev`), (b) rebuild happy-web-dev from worktree, (c) restart happy-daemon-dev via /root/bin/safe-daemon-restart.sh dev. QA verification matrix: AC1 (real-time bg-task render desktop+mobile), AC2 (web close+reopen restores 'claude babbling' indicator within 5s), AC3 ('Last Updated' refreshes — depends on pipeline 7.1's session-alive cadence fix), AC4 (no regression on prior fixes), AC5 (Playwright capture of WS frames showing the connect-time ephemeral snapshot). Specifically for pipeline 7.2: open DevTools → Network → WS during reopen, look for an `ephemeral` frame with `type:'activity', id:<sid>, thinking:true` arriving within ~100ms of socket reconnect (no need to wait for next heartbeat).

diff_stats.justification_for_overage: Most of the new symbols are pure refactors required by `pretool-quality-gate.py` (max function size 30 lines, max nesting depth 3). The original socket.ts had a 140-line connection handler with depth-5 nesting; original sessionUpdateHandler had a 287-line exported function. The hook hard-blocks ANY edit to a file violating these thresholds, regardless of whether the edit touches the violating area. BA spec Section 8 anticipates this: 'Each Dev pipeline must scope edits to specific line ranges and may hit pretool-quality-gate.py. Plan minimum-diff patches.' I split each file's mega-functions into focused sub-30-line helpers preserving exact semantics, then added the new pipeline 7.2 logic. The functional addition (new module + 3 call sites) is ~30 lines; the remaining ~58 net lines are forced refactor.

self_verification.smoke_check: skipped (no executable acceptance criteria runnable from this pipeline alone — pipeline 7.2 only takes effect end-to-end after pipelines 7.1 and 7.3 also land, with rebuilds of happy-server-dev + happy-web-dev + restart of happy-daemon-dev, which is orchestrator-coordinated)
self_verification.notes: Pre-existing TypeScript error in sessionCache.ts:42 (`Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'Timeout'` for setInterval return) is unrelated — that file was not modified by this pipeline. Verified via `git diff --stat packages/happy-server/sources/app/presence/sessionCache.ts` returning empty. The pre-existing error does not block server runtime (this is a TS compile-only error from `--noEmit`).

recommendations: Pre-existing sessionCache.ts:42 TS error should be tracked separately (not in this pipeline's scope). Suggested fix: `let batchTimer: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null` instead of `: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null` then assigning a number-typed return.

Future cycle: if multi-process happy-server is ever deployed, swap thinkingCache's in-memory Map for Redis to share state across instances. Public API of recordThinking/clearThinking/getActivitySnapshotForUser was designed to make this swap drop-in.

Future cycle: consider extending `getActivitySnapshotForUser` to also include sessions with `pending RPC` (e.g. permission_required) so reconnects can also instantly restore that indicator — currently out-of-scope for 5.19.
